Before using the app, please read and accept the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy. They explain what the app does, what it does not do, which components are third-party, and where the data stays.

TERMS OF USE

Last updated: September 20, 2026.

1. ACCEPTANCE

By installing, accessing or using the PhotoID RT application (the "App"), you (the "User") declare that you have read, understood and agreed to these Terms of Use. If you do not agree with any provision, do not use the App.

2. NATURE AND PURPOSE

SUPPORT TOOL. NOT VALIDATED FOR CLINICAL USE.

PhotoID RT assists the photographic record of radiotherapy positioning. The App is NOT a medical device, does NOT diagnose, does NOT measure, does NOT interpret medical images and does NOT replace professional judgement.

What the App builds is the ACCESSIBILITY LAYER: the interface that organises capture by category, stores the files and assembles the positioning sheet with its Time-Out page.

Label text recognition and barcode reading are NOT authored by us: they are performed by Google ML Kit, a third-party component embedded in the App. We did not develop that component and we claim no authorship over it.

Fields filled in by that recognition are SUGGESTIONS and require checking by the User before any use. The printed sheet is the responsibility of the team that issued it.

3. INTENDED USERS

Radiotherapy professionals — technologists, medical physicists and physicians — acting in the regular exercise of their duties, under the rules of their institution and their professional boards.

4. USER RESPONSIBILITIES

The User is responsible for checking patient identification before generating or printing any sheet; for obtaining patient consent for the photographic record according to institutional policy; for keeping the device controlled and protected; and for complying with applicable law, including data protection legislation.

The healthcare institution is the DATA CONTROLLER for patient data. The App is a tool operated by and under the responsibility of that institution.

5. WARRANTY AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

The App is provided "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, express or implied, including warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. This mirrors sections 7 and 8 of the Apache License 2.0, under which the App is licensed.

To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the authors and copyright holders shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages arising from the use of or inability to use the App, even if advised of the possibility of such damages.

It is for the User and the institution to determine whether the App is appropriate for their own use, and to assume the risks of that decision.

6. LICENCE AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

The source code of the App is published under the APACHE LICENSE 2.0. You may use, reproduce, modify and redistribute the App and derivative works under the terms of that licence, whose full text ships with the package in the LICENSE file.

When redistributing, section 4(d) of the licence requires you to preserve the attribution notices in the NOTICE file, and section 4(b) requires you to mark the files you changed.

The App incorporates third-party components, each under its own licence: Google ML Kit, under the ML Kit terms (proprietary, free to use), and components under Apache License 2.0 and BSD. The full list, with authorship, licence and version, is in the NOTICE file and on the Settings, About screen.

TRADEMARKS ARE NOT INCLUDED IN THE LICENCE. Per section 6 of the Apache License 2.0, the names and logos "Radioterapia.AI" and "PhotoID RT" are not licensed for identifying derivative products.

7. TWO REGIMES, THE SAME CODE

They do not overlap, and the distinction is who deploys it and for what.

PUBLISHED SOURCE: educational material. Not a medical device and not validated for clinical use. Whoever downloads, modifies and deploys it is responsible for their own build and for validation in their own service.

INSTITUTIONAL BUILD: when a healthcare service compiles, validates and deploys the App for its own use, it assumes the corresponding responsibilities, including documented validation and record retention under the applicable standard.

8. CHANGES

The authors may amend these Terms. Material changes are announced in the App. Continued use after the announcement implies acceptance.

9. TERMINATION

The User may stop using the App at any time by uninstalling it. Termination does not affect the rights granted by the Apache License 2.0 over source already obtained.

10. GOVERNING LAW

11. BUILT-IN SYNCHRONIZATION

From version 4.0 on, the Application includes a function that sends the files recorded on the device to destinations configured by the institution. It is OPTIONAL and ships DISABLED.

Enabling it is the institution's decision, and with it the institution takes on the choice of destination, its adequacy under the applicable law, and the security of the network the files travel through. The Application defines no destination, operates no server and receives no copy of what is sent.

The function is one-way and deletes nothing at the destination. Data handling is described in the Privacy Policy.

12. CONTACT

Questions about these Terms may be sent through radioterapia.ai.

PRIVACY POLICY

Last updated: September 20, 2026.

1. GENERAL PRINCIPLE: DATA STAYS ON THE TABLET

NO patient data is sent to the authors of the App, to any server of ours, to third-party APIs or to the cloud. There is no account, no login and no telemetry.

The photos and generated PDFs stay in the tablet's own storage. Transfer to the institution's server, when it configures one, is done either by an external synchronization app OR by the Application's own synchronization, described in section 12. In neither case is the destination ours: it is always an address the institution itself provides.

2. WHAT THE APP DOES ON THE NETWORK

We do not say the Application is "100 percent offline", because that would not be accurate. It uses the network in three situations, and the first two always happen inside the institution's own network:

(a) PRINTING: it sends the sheet PDF to a network printer configured by the service.

(b) PATIENT DATABASE AND REVIEW: when the service configures a shared folder, the App reads the patient database in CSV from it, and reads photos already stored on the institution server. That communication uses signed SMB, and encrypted SMB when the configuration declares SMB3.

(c) BUILT-IN SYNCHRONIZATION: when the institution enables it, the Application sends the files in the storage folder to the destinations it configures — file server, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, or a folder in a cloud service already installed on the device. It ships DISABLED. See section 12.

Outside these three situations, the Application does not access the network. The first two do not leave the institution's network; the third goes only to the destination the institution itself configures, and exists only if the institution enables it.

3. RECOGNITION RUNS ON THE DEVICE

Label text recognition and barcode reading are performed by Google ML Kit EMBEDDED in the App, processing on the tablet itself. The label image is NOT sent to Google or to any external service for that processing.

4. DATA PROCESSED

Clinical data entered or captured by the User: photographs, name, record number, date of birth, sex, attending physician, machine, treatment site, risks and notes. They stay on the tablet and, when the institution configures it, in its own network folder.

Local technical data: an audit log of actions taken in the App, kept on the device for the traceability of the institution.

5. DATA PROTECTION COMPLIANCE

THE HEALTHCARE INSTITUTION is the data controller. It defines the purpose and means of processing, answers for data subject rights and must appoint its own Data Protection Officer.

The authors of the App have no access to the data processed, do not receive it and do not act as processors on behalf of the institution: the App runs entirely on the institution infrastructure.

6. PERMISSIONS REQUESTED

CAMERA: to capture the photographs. It is the central function of the App.

STORAGE, including all-files access: to write photos and PDFs to a visible folder on the device, so that they survive uninstallation and so that the institution synchronisation app can read them.

NETWORK: to talk to the printer and to the institution file server, as described in section 2.

The App does NOT request MICROPHONE, does NOT request LOCATION, does NOT request CONTACTS and does NOT request CALENDAR. Voice control was implemented and then removed: the guarantee that audio would never leave the device only holds from Android 13 onwards, and the App must work across the whole tablet fleet.

7. SECURITY

Passwords for the institution network are stored encrypted on the device (Android secure storage). Physical protection of the tablet, screen lock and control over who uses it are the responsibility of the institution.

8. CHILDREN

The App is intended for professional use. Photographs of underage patients follow the consent policy of the institution and applicable law.

9. INTERNATIONAL TRANSFER

It depends on the destination the institution configures, and on that alone. With synchronization disabled, or pointed at a server on the institution's own network, there is no international transfer. If the institution points synchronization at a cloud service, the files come to be stored where that service stores them, under its terms. That is the institution's decision: the Application has no destination of its own and sends nothing to the authors.

10. RETENTION

Files remain for as long as the institution keeps them. The App does not delete patient data on its own. Uninstalling the App removes data held in its private area; photos written to the public folder survive, provided all-files access was granted.

11. UPDATES TO THIS POLICY

This Policy may be updated. Material changes are announced in the App before taking effect.

12. THE APPLICATION'S OWN SYNCHRONIZATION

DISABLED OUT OF THE BOX. While the master switch is off, the Application does not use the network on its own: there is no background service, no connection attempt, and no data leaves the device.

When enabled, the Application copies the files in the storage folder — photographs, PDFs and the patient base — to the destinations the institution configures. What is sent is the same as what is already recorded on the tablet.

IT IS ONE-WAY AND NEVER DELETES. The Application writes at the destination; it does not remove, does not rename and does not bring anything back.

Access credentials are encrypted on the device, in the Android secure storage, and do not travel with the configuration transfer package. The authors of the Application have no access to any destination, receive no copy and operate no server.

13. CONTACT AND DATA PROTECTION OFFICER

Questions about this Policy may be sent through radioterapia.ai. The controlling healthcare institution must appoint its own Data Protection Officer; the authors of the App do not act as the institution officer.

Remove this destination? The record of what was already sent is forgotten too — what is already on the server is not deleted.
The server name or IP, nothing else — no slashes and no folder. In "\\\\SRV-FILES\\rt\\photos" the server is SRV-FILES. If the name does not resolve on the tablet\'s network, use the IP.

The share is the FIRST folder of the network path, the one the server publishes. In "\\\\SRV\\rt\\photos\\2026" the share is "rt" and the rest goes in the remote folder. Administrative shares ending in "$" are accepted.
Just the login or ID, without the domain attached. Do not write "DOMAIN\\user" or "user@domain" — the domain has its own field just below, and the app assembles the authentication.
The Active Directory domain, when the account is a domain account. It is usually the part before the backslash in the Windows login. Leave empty on a server without a domain.

The folder inside the destination where the tablet\'s structure is reproduced. Leave empty to write at the root. The per-patient folders are created inside it, with the same names they have on the tablet.
The full folder address, with http:// or https://. It is the same address the browser opens. On self-hosted cloud services the password is usually an app password, not the login one.

Pick the folder with the system picker, inside the cloud app your service already uses and is already signed in to. No password goes through this app. If the cloud app is reinstalled or the account changes, pick the folder again.

When on, the app writes straight into the final folder without checking the folders above it. This solves the common hospital case: the account can write at the destination but cannot READ the folders above — and the check would fail on a folder that is not even the destination. Turn it off only if the server refuses the direct write.
